statement: The 2010 National Football Conference (NFC) Championship Game was an American football game played between the Green Bay Packers and the Chicago Bears on January 23, 2011, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois, United States.
The Bears–Packers rivalry is one of the longest and most storied rivalries in National Football League (NFL) history.
The two teams had only ever met in the postseason once, in 1941.
The Packers and Bears both play in the NFC North division.
The Packers and Bears battled throughout the regular season for the division title.
The Bears pulled away late in the season to secure the title and the second seed in the playoffs.
The Packers secured a Wild Card berth.
The Packers beat the Philadelphia Eagles and Atlanta Falcons to advance to the NFC Championship Game.
The Bears had a first-round bye before beating the Seattle Seahawks in the Divisional round.
With their higher seeding, the Bears hosted the Packers at Soldier Field for the NFC Championship Game.
The Packers took an early 14–0 lead.
The game became a defensive struggle.
Each team combined for 17 punts and five interceptions.
After Bears' quarterback Jay Cutler was injured, back-up Todd Collins was put in.
Todd Collins was not effective.
The Bears then put in Caleb Hanie, their third-string quarterback.
Caleb Hanie led the offense on a touchdown drive to bring the score to 14–7.
After a Packers punt, Hanie threw a short pass that was intercepted by B. J. Raji.
B. J. Raji returned the interception for a touchdown.
Hanie led another touchdown drive.
The Bears defense forced another punt by the Packers.
Hanie threw a second interception, this time to Sam Shields.
The second interception by Sam Shields effectively ended the game.
The Packers advanced to Super Bowl XLV.
The Packers beat the Pittsburgh Steelers to secure their 13th championship in team history.
The Green Bay Packers began the 2010 NFL season having reached the playoffs in the previous season.
The Packers lost to the Arizona Cardinals in a Wild Card game in the previous season.
The Packers started 2010 with a record of 3–3.
The 3–3 record included a loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 3.
The 3–3 record included two other overtime losses.
The Packers then went on a four-game winning streak.
The Packers lost three of four games to bring their record to 8–6.
The Packers needed to win their last two games of the year to make the postseason.
The Packers blew-out the New York Giants.
The Packers beat the Bears in the last game of the season to secure the sixth seed in the playoffs.
The Packers offense and defense ranked in the top 10 in yards and points.
The Packers travelled to play the Philadelphia Eagles in the Wild Card round.
The Packers beat the Philadelphia Eagles 21–16.
In the Divisional Round, the Packers blew-out the Atlanta Falcons 48–21.
The Packers advanced to the NFC Championship Game.
The Bears went 7–9 in the 2009 season.
The Bears had not made the playoffs for the previous three years.
The Bears won the first three games of the season.
The Bears lost three out of four games after winning the first three.
The Bears then went 7–2 over the remaining nine games of the season.
The 7–2 run included a five-game win streak.
The 7–2 run included the aforementioned loss to the Packers in the last game of the regular season.
With their 11–5 record, the Bears beat-out the Packers for the NFC North division title.
The Bears were given the second seed in the playoffs.
The first-seeded team in the playoffs was the Falcons.
The Bears were led by their defense.
The Bears' defense was ranked in the top five in points allowed.
The Bears' defense was the second best team against the run.
The Bears had a bye week in the first round of the playoffs.
The Bears hosted the Seattle Seahawks in the Divisional round.
The Bears advanced to the NFC Championship Game after beating the Seahawks 35–24.
With their higher seeding, the Bears were scheduled to host the Packers at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois, for the NFC Championship Game on January 23, 2011.
The Packers were 3.5 point favorites.
The Bears won the coin toss.
The Bears elected to defer their decision to the second half.
Because the Bears deferred, the Packers were given the option to kickoff or receive the kickoff.
The Packers began the game with possession of the ball after receiving the kickoff.
On the first two plays of the drive, Rodgers completed passes of 22 and 26 yards to Greg Jennings.
After two short plays, Rodgers completed a 22-yard pass to Jordy Nelson.
On the next play, Rodgers ran in a one-yard touchdown to give the Packers a 7–0 lead.
The next five consecutive drives, three by the Bears and two by the Packers, ended in punts.
After taking possession at mid-field, the Packers drove 49 yards in 5 plays.
The drive was capped off by a four-yard rushing touchdown by James Starks.
The touchdown increased the Packers' lead to 14–0.
Three more drives, two by the Bears and one by the Packers, ended in punts.
The Packers drove to mid-field on their next drive.
Rodgers threw a pass intended for Donald Driver that was intercepted by Lance Briggs.
Just one play later, Jay Cutler threw a deep pass towards Johnny Knox that was intercepted by Sam Shields.
The play was reviewed to verify whether the pass was intercepted.
The call on the field was confirmed.
Cutler was injured on the play.
The Packers kneeled the ball to run out the rest of the game clock in the first half.
The Bears started the second half with the ball.
The Bears went three-and-out and punted.
The Packers drove down the field to the six-yard line.
Rodgers threw a pass that was intercepted by Brian Urlacher.
Brian Urlacher returned the ball to mid-field.
Rodgers was able to tackle Urlacher, preventing a possible defensive touchdown.
The Bears again went three-and-out.
Collins was in as quarterback for Cutler.
Cutler's earlier knee injury ended up keeping him out for the rest of the game.
The drive included an interception by the Packers that was reversed via instant replay.
On the next drive, the Packers punted to the Bears.
The Bears went three-and-out again.
After a Bears' punt, the Packers then went three-and-out.
The Bears replaced Collins for Caleb Hanie.
Caleb Hanie led the Bears on an eight-play, 67-yard drive.
The drive ended in a short touchdown run to bring the score to 14–7.
The next three drives, two by the Packers and one by the Bears, ended in punts after short drives.
The Bears took over on their own 10-yard line.
After a short rush by Matt Forte, Hanie threw a short pass that was intercepted by B. J. Raji.
B. J. Raji returned the interception for a touchdown.
The touchdown increased the Packers lead to 21–7.
The Bears got the ball, down by two touchdowns with six minutes left in the game.
Hanie led a quick scoring drive.
The scoring drive was capped by a 35-yard touchdown pass to Bennett.
With a little over four-and-a-half minutes left in the game, the Bears kicked the ball off to the Packers.
The Packers went three-and-out while moving backwards one yard on the drive.
The Bears took over after the Packers punt with almost three minutes left in the game.
The Bears were down 21–14.
The Bears needed a touchdown to tie or win.
The Bears drove 44 yards to the Packers 29-yard line.
On fourth down and five yards to go, with under a minute left in the game, Hanie threw a deep pass that was intercepted by Sam Shields.
Rodgers and the Packers' offense came onto the field.
Rodgers and the Packers' offense knelt down once to end the game.
The stadium for the game was Soldier Field, Chicago, Illinois.
The game time was 3:05 p.m. EST/2:00 p.m. CST.
The weather was 20°F.
The wind was at 14 mph.
The attendance was 62,377.
The game was televised on Fox.
The announcers were Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Pam Oliver, and Chris Myers.
GB scored a touchdown with Aaron Rodgers 1-yard run at 10:50 in the first quarter.
Mason Crosby kicked the extra point for GB's first touchdown.
The score became Packers 7–0.
The drive for GB's first touchdown was 7 plays, 84 yards, and took 4:10.
GB scored a touchdown with James Starks 4-yard run at 11:13 in the second quarter.
Mason Crosby kicked the extra point for GB's second touchdown.
The score became Packers 14–0.
The drive for GB's second touchdown was 5 plays, 44 yards, and took 2:53.
There were no scoring plays in the third quarter.
CHI scored a touchdown with Chester Taylor 1-yard run at 12:02 in the fourth quarter.
Robbie Gould kicked the extra point for CHI's first touchdown.
The score became Packers 14–7.
The drive for CHI's first touchdown was 8 plays, 67 yards, and took 3:55.
GB scored a touchdown with B. J. Raji 18-yard interception return at 6:04 in the fourth quarter.
Mason Crosby kicked the extra point for GB's interception return touchdown.
The score became Packers 21–7.
CHI scored a touchdown with Earl Bennett 35-yard pass from Caleb Hanie at 4:43 in the fourth quarter.
Robbie Gould kicked the extra point for CHI's second touchdown.
The score became Packers 21–14.
The drive for CHI's second touchdown was 4 plays, 60 yards, and took 1:21.

Post-game analysis centered on the competitive nature of the game, the teams' historic rivalry, and performances by individual players.
After the Packers jumped to a 14–0 lead, the game became more defensive.
Over the entire game, both teams combined for 17 punts and five interceptions.
Each team had only two offensive scoring drives a piece.
Each team was also poor on third down.
The Packers and Bears only converted three times combined on third down.
For the Bears, Forte carried the offensive load, accumulating 160 yards rushing and receiving combined.
Matt Forte's 10 receptions were a franchise playoff record.
For the Packers, Jennings had a productive game, catching eight passes for 130 yards.
Rodgers threw for 244 yards.
Rodgers rushed for a touchdown.
Rodgers threw two interceptions.
Rodgers completed barely 50% of his passes.
Shields secured two interceptions.
One of Shields' interceptions was on the final drive to seal the victory.
Raji's interception return for a touchdown was highlighted as the key play of the game.
Punter Tim Masthay was also highlighted for his success in limiting the productivity of the Bears' star returner, Devin Hester.
Devin Hester would go on to be elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Masthay was able to maximize ball placement, hangtime, and direction to make it difficult for Hester to return the ball.
Masthay's punting also provided the Packers' coverage team the opportunity to make a tackle.
Another key point of discussion after the game was the impact of Cutler's injury and the performance of the Bears' back-up quarterbacks.
Cutler received much criticism for not continuing to play.
Cutler had been relatively ineffective.
The Bears' coaches were the ones that decided to pull him off the field.
Cutler's injury was confirmed after the game.
Collins was completely ineffective coming in for two drives.
Hanie was able to come in and move the offense.
Hanie threw two interceptions.
Hanie led two scoring drives.
Hanie gave the Bears an opportunity for a comeback.
It was reported that some Bears' players questioned why Hanie was not the second-string quarterback.
The Packers admitted after the game they had not done any preparation on Hanie.
The Packers admitted after the game they did not know much about Hanie.
Multiple sources highlighted the importance of this game to the teams' rivalry.
The game was important because it was only the second time the teams played in the postseason.
The game was important because the winner moved on to the Super Bowl.
With the victory, the Packers advanced to Super Bowl XLV against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
It was their first Super Bowl berth since the 1997 NFL season.
After the game, Packers defensive back Charles Woodson predicted a Packers' Super Bowl victory.
Charles Woodson referenced president Barack Obama's Chicago roots.
Charles Woodson referenced the traditional visit to the White House by the NFL champions.
Charles Woodson stated "The President don't want to come watch the Super Bowl? Guess what? We're gonna see him!"
The Packers then went on to beat the Steelers 31–25.
The Packers secured the franchise's 13th championship.
The Packers became only the second team in NFL history to win a Super Bowl as the sixth seed.
The Packers were the first team to do so from the National Football Conference.
Rodgers was named the Super Bowl Most Valuable Player.
Rodgers threw three touchdowns and over 300 yards passing in the Super Bowl.
The Packers would continue their success throughout the 2010s.
The Packers made the playoffs each of the next six seasons.
The 2010 NFC Championship Game marked the pinnacle for the Bears in the 2010s.
The Bears missed the playoffs for the next seven seasons after 2010.
The Bears only made the postseason once more during the decade, in 2018.
The Bears and Packers have one of the longest and most storied rivalries in NFL history.
The rivalry spans over 100 years.
The two teams had only ever met in the playoffs once before 2010.
In 1941, the Bears beat the Packers 33–14.
The Bears won the 1941 NFL Championship Game against the New York Giants.
This NFC Championship Game immediately became a noted part of the teams' rivalry.
In 2025, Sports Illustrated identified the game as the best in the history of the rivalry.
Raji's interception return for a touchdown was the first score of his career.
Raji's interception return for a touchdown was ranked as one of the 50 greatest sports moments in Wisconsin history by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel in 2020.
This game, along with the entire playoff run and Super Bowl victory for the Packers, helped solidify Rodgers status as a premier starting quarterback in the NFL.
It ended up being the only NFC Championship Game victory for Rodgers.
Rodgers would go on to lose four straight NFC Championship Games after 2010.
For the Bears, the game has been characterized as one of the worst defeats in team history.
Cutler returned the next year and had one of his best statistical seasons.
Questions regarding the severity of Cutler's injury during the game and whether he could have played persisted for years.
